clue.text: Bring up opportunity for picture

blocks.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
a window of opportunity, or simply a window

explanation.surface: Someone suggests raising the chance to take a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is the old word for a film; this one is Hitchcock's 1954 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear Window is a Hitchcock movie, and a picture is an informal term for a film.

clue.text: Cancel toll again?

blocks.note: first meaning: revoke a law
second meaning, read as RE- plus PEAL: ring the bells once more

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, split as a prefix meaning again plus a word for ringing bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a statute is to revoke or annul it, and re-peal would be to ring out a second time.

clue.text: What produces nice aroma when brewed?

definitions.text: What produces nice aroma when brewed?

indicators.note: brewing stirs and mixes ingredients, so the letters before it are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what makes a lovely smell once it has been brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the brewed letters of the two words give a coffee that does indeed smell nice.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a brewed coffee that gives off a pleasant smell.

clue.text: Wild cows in wrong place for dairy?

indicators.note: wild things are out of control, so the letters that follow run loose into a new order

blocks.note: these six letters are rearranged
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Cows that have gone wild have wandered somewhere unsuitable for milking.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisconsin is known as America's Dairyland, hence the question mark on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state is famous for cheese and milk production, earning the nickname America's Dairyland.

clue.text: Independent award following term of town crier

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the last letter of town
I is the abbreviation for Independent
the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An independent prize-giving follows the term of office of a town crier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town crier' looks like one official; the crier is a figure from Greek myth. 'Following' puts the honour after the letter from town.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobe, in Greek myth, wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned into a weeping rock.

clue.text: Middle of sturdy bridge crossed by extremely grumpy country runners

indicators.note: only the central part is wanted, so the outer letters of the synonym are discarded
extremes are the far ends, so only the first and last letters are kept
something crossed by another has it lying over both sides, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: solid means sturdy
the first and last letters of grumpy
an arch is a bridge

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered pair of cross-country athletes runs across the centre of a solid bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country runners' suggests athletes on a cross-country course; it means the few who run a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is a small group of people who hold power and govern a state.

clue.text: American bought retro garment

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
got means obtained or bought

explanation.surface: A US shopper picked up a vintage piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A toga was the loose outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Lead in Hitchcock film dropped by a musical drama

indicators.note: the first letter is let fall from its place and set down next to the following word

blocks.note: Rope is a 1948 Hitchcock film
the leading letter of the film title
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star of a Hitchcock movie is replaced by a song-and-dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: The film's opening letter drops out of its place and lands beside 'a', at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and sung throughout.

clue.text: More than one donkey helps to surround bird

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: aids means helps
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Several donkeys help to round up a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkey' is the slang sense of a fool, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a stupid person, and donkey is likewise a colloquial term for a fool.

clue.text: Skinny piece of tin foil

indicators.note: a piece is a part of something, so the letters are a portion of the following words

blocks.note: sits across the two words

explanation.surface: A thin scrap of aluminium wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like an adjective describing the piece; it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: The skinny is informal slang for the inside facts or details on something.

clue.text: I don't know about replacing a clasp

indicators.note: replacing means putting one thing in the position of another, here in place of the letter a

blocks.note: a quiz contestant says pass when they don't know
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone admits ignorance on how to swap out a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp someone is to hold or squeeze them tightly, which is to press them.

clue.text: One sporting informal top with French zip, covered in gold

indicators.note: something covered in another is wrapped inside it, so the pieces sit within

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
rien is French for nothing
a tee is an informal T-shirt

explanation.surface: Someone wears a casual T-shirt with a French zipper and gold trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' suggests wearing; it marks the definition as a sportsperson. Zip is slang for nothing, so French zip is rien.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer takes part in the sport of racing across country with a map and compass.

clue.text: A Russian plane over China

blocks.note: taken as written
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Soviet fighter flies over the Chinese mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: China is a country in the surface but rhyming slang in the answer: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, and amigo is Spanish for a friend or pal.

clue.text: Eastern US industry demolished complex

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
labor is the American spelling of labour, meaning work or industry
to demolish food is to eat it all, so ate

explanation.surface: Eastern American manufacturing has torn down a building complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a noun for a group of buildings; it is the adjective for intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate and detailed, with many interrelated parts.

clue.text: Increase cast, scouring The Fifth Element

indicators.note: scouring scrubs something away, here the letter in fifth position of the first word
cast means thrown or moulded anew, so the remaining letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film studio enlarges its cast and searches through the film The Fifth Element.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fifth Element is a 1997 film, but here the fifth is a letter position and Element alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a chemical element, atomic number 33, notorious as a poison.

clue.text: Flow of Red River accordingly entering cave to the north

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so these pieces sit within the cave word
in a down answer, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a den is a cave or lair
the Elbe is a central European river
so means therefore or accordingly

explanation.surface: The Red River flows into a cave as it heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red River' reads as a place name, but the definition stops at Red, meaning blood. Everything then runs upward from the bottom of the light.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is a flow of blood from the nose, and red stands in for blood.

clue.text: E.g. man's offer to host games

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a bid is an offer
PE is physical education, school games

explanation.surface: A man's proposal to stage some sports fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, and a biped is any two-footed animal, man being one example.

clue.text: Shock secures around 50 fish

indicators.note: around signals one piece placed so as to enclose another

blocks.note: binds means ties or secures
L is the Roman numeral for 50
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An alarming report says fifty fish have been captured.
explanation.definitionFit: To blindside someone is to catch them unawares, to shock them with an unexpected blow.

clue.text: Male – scratch that, males – involved in each year's events

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it, so these pieces go within

blocks.note: pa is per annum, each year
he is the male pronoun
no is a word cancelling what was just said
men are males

explanation.surface: A speaker corrects themselves mid-sentence about men attending yearly events.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make it look like a self-correction, but the correction itself supplies letters too.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are observable occurrences or happenings, a more formal word for events.

clue.text: Blue queen interrupting light brown queen

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another, so it sits inside

blocks.note: sand is a pale yellowish-brown colour
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: One queen disturbs a blonde one, both described by their colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour, among the other colours here; it is the verb meaning to spend recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is British slang for spending it wastefully, which is to squander it.

clue.text: Hunt for vegetarian alternative

blocks.note: first meaning: a famous Leicestershire fox hunt
second meaning: a meat-free protein brand

explanation.walkthrough: The Quorn is an English hunt in Leicestershire; Quorn is also a brand of mycoprotein meat substitute, ironically named after the village.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a long-established fox-hunting pack and to a mycoprotein food used instead of meat.

clue.text: This might be high like NY's?

definitions.text: This might be high like NY's?

indicators.note: someone high is intoxicated and not straight, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that might be as lofty as New York's.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and its last letters rearranged spell it: New York's skyline is famously high.
explanation.definitionFit: A skyline is the outline of buildings against the sky, and Manhattan's is famously tall.

clue.text: New arrangement of steel bar manufacturers

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a fresh order, so the letters of the metal are reordered

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steelworks makes a fresh layout for its iron bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests metal, given the steel; here it is a chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestlé is the food company that makes chocolate bars such as KitKat.

clue.text: Wise expert accepting day pass

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece is received inside another

blocks.note: able means skilled or expert
D is the abbreviation for day
a visa is a pass permitting entry to a country

explanation.surface: A sage specialist takes on a one-day travel permit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise course of action is a prudent, sensible one, which is to say advisable.

clue.text: Classical beauty spots shunned by English

indicators.note: something shunned is kept away, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: venues are spots or locations
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English person avoids a classically beautiful woman with blemishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like pimples beside 'beauty'; it means places.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus was the Roman goddess of love and beauty, an emblem of beauty from the classical world.

clue.text: Male second name

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A man's middle name.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and the word also describes an all-male event.

clue.text: Frame fish, having caught 14

indicators.note: catching something holds it fast inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an eel is a fish
the answer to 14 is a chemical element whose symbol is As

explanation.surface: A trophy fish is put in a frame after being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to the 14-across answer; its chemical symbol is the letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand or frame used to hold a painter's canvas.

clue.text: Gender-neutral pronoun used by Doctor Psmith, say

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
one is an impersonal pronoun with no gender

explanation.surface: A doctor called Psmith uses inclusive pronouns.
explanation.walkthrough: Psmith is a P. G. Wodehouse character, a member of the Drones Club of idle young men-about-town.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is an idler, and Psmith belongs to Wodehouse's Drones Club of leisured gentlemen.

clue.text: Brazilian footballer: someone who looks to be in reverse gear

indicators.note: in reverse means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Dunga captained Brazil to the 1994 World Cup
a seer is one who sees

explanation.surface: A Brazilian player looks as if he is driving backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse gear' reads as a car phrase, but gear is the definition, meaning clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are bib overalls, and gear is informal for clothes.

clue.text: Unable to complete tasks in record time

blocks.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone fails to finish their jobs in record-breaking time.
explanation.definitionFit: An inept person lacks skill and is incompetent, so cannot get jobs done.

clue.text: What might follow failure to cut international break

indicators.note: cutting something removes it, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: a student who fails an exam has to take it again
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: After failing to make the national team, a player takes time off.
explanation.walkthrough: A resit is a second attempt at an exam one has failed, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a pause or break from activity.

clue.text: Doctor's obscene drug price

blocks.note: adult content is obscene or explicit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A physician charges an outrageous sum for medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician; it is the verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to falsify or tamper with it, which is what adulterating a substance does.
